The Green Corridor

two mirrors, one candle, seen from above
turns to close — angle — throat —

The tunnel the Hall of Mirrors is named for

A kaleidoscope is two mirrors and a secret. Upstairs you look through the small end and the secret keeps itself. Here the lid is off: the same two mirrors, seen from above, with one candle set between them.

The flames walk away down the line. Each one is a real reflection of the one before it, and silvered glass keeps only most of the light — and keeps the red least. So the far end of the corridor is bottle-green, and then it is nothing at all.

Move the mirrors. Tilt them. Take one away.

Nothing here is measured. The green is a feeling, honestly earned: a little less light at every bounce, and the warm end of it going first.
